answer: Anchor every agent identity to one physical address. A postal carrier delivers a one-time code to the timber mailbox post and signs the receipt, which is published on chain; that address cannot anchor another identity for a year. A second cedar mailbox does not help without another household to receive, staff, and pay for it, so each fake identity costs rent, travel, and a carrier visit. Without this anchor the registry dissolves into a nebula of disposable accounts, but with it a Sybil operator pays a real-world price per identity while an honest agent pays once.
